text:
kevin: heads-up — ran into a nasty cross-platform async issue when integrating the Python SDK in a Windows service test. Symptoms: weird "Cannot run the event loop while another loop is running" errors and occasional "Task attached to a different loop" from httpcore. repro below.

kevin: minimal repro (simplified):
```py
# library code (current SDK behavior)
class Client:
    def __init__(self):
        self._ac = httpx.AsyncClient()

def sync_entry():
    c = Client()
    asyncio.run(c._ac.get("https://example.com"))
```

kevin: running the above inside an existing asyncio context (e.g., uvloop or a test harness that already has a loop) throws because asyncio.run creates a new loop and disallows a running loop in the current thread. On Windows the default loop policy is different (Proactor) and mixing policies plus creating AsyncClient early binds transports to the wrong loop.

ivy: ugh, yeah. libraries must not call asyncio.run or manage the loop. Also creating AsyncClient eagerly is problematic — httpx/httpcore stores references to loop/task factories. Good patterns: 1) never call asyncio.run inside library code, 2) offer an async factory to create transport on the active loop, 3) provide a sync wrapper that runs a dedicated background thread event loop for blocking callers.

sam: we saw a related flaky test in CI when a sample app used a sync helper that called asyncio.new_event_loop() + set_event_loop + run_until_complete. When pytest-asyncio or anyio had their own loop, things went sideways. Best practice is: if you need sync API, spin up a single background thread with its own loop and marshal calls across with run_coroutine_threadsafe. Example helper we use internally:
```py
class SyncClient:
    def __init__(self, *args, **kw):
        self._loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
        self._thread = Thread(target=self._loop.run_forever, daemon=True)
        self._thread.start()
        self._client = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(httpx.AsyncClient(), self._loop).result()

    def request(self, *a, **k):
        fut = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(self._client.get(*a, **k), self._loop)
        return fut.result()
```

sam: note: be careful to aclose clients and stop the loop on process shutdown; otherwise threads linger and tests hang.

kevin: good call. Another wrinkle we hit: changing asyncio loop policy at runtime (e.g., switching to uvloop) after the AsyncClient exists leads to subtle errors because transports were created with the original loop policy. So creating AsyncClient before policy switch is brittle. We should document that users must set loop policy before instantiating SDK.

ivy: suggestions for SDK changes: 1) remove eager httpx.AsyncClient creation from __init__, 2) add `@classmethod async def create(...)` that constructs transport in running loop, 3) add `def sync_wrapper()` that returns SyncClient, 4) detect and raise helpful error if client is created when an incompatible loop policy is in effect (maybe detect uvloop vs default?).

sam: also add tests in CI matrix for Windows (GitHub Actions windows-latest), macOS, and Linux with uvloop. Add pytest jobs that exercise sync wrapper and background-thread pattern, plus tests that switch loop policy mid-process to confirm we error rather than silently break.

kevin: i opened an issue with a tiny repro and links to Win CI logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/2633 — includes a small pytest and Windows GH workflow that reproduces the problem.

qa-bot: Created issue #2633 (redwood-inference/python-sdk): "Windows loop policy + eager AsyncClient creation causes runtime errors and test hangs" assigned to @ivy.

ivy: i'll take a patch. quick plan: implement async create(), add SyncClient wrapper, document loop-policy ordering, add CI jobs, and include a deprecation warning if __init__ creates AsyncClient on import. I'll open a PR with tests and a sample snippet for running in Windows services.

sam: thanks — one more tiny DX idea: add a short troubleshooting section in SDK README called "Async gotchas" that lists: do not use asyncio.run in library code, prefer async factories, avoid top-level AsyncClient instances, and patterns for FastAPI lifespan and pytest fixtures. That should cut down on support noise.

kevin: agreed. i'll update our sample apps to use the SyncClient for quickstarts so Windows users don't hit this immediately. thanks all.
